chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while he was in prayer, so I said, 'Peace be upon you.' He said, 'Peace be upon you.' I said, 'How did you spend the morning?' and he remained silent. Then, when he finished, I asked him, 'Does one return the greeting while he is in prayer?' He said, 'Yes, like what was said to him.'

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to say Salam to someone who is currently praying?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of responding to greetings during prayer, establishing that one may reply with 'Alaikum al-Salam' without invalidating the prayer. It highlights the distinction between the obligatory recitation and the permissible verbal responses, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that brevity and appropriateness are key when interrupting the flow of worship for social courtesy.
